The clinical examination was unremarkable except for a systolic murmur. There was no more weakness in the legs. The ECG showed AF with T-negativities in III. Laboratory tests showed a haemoglobin of 88 g/L, leucocytes of 15.9 x109/L, CRP of 60 mg/L (ref.:<10 mg/L), creatinine of 198 µmol/l (ref.:<104 µmol/l). Blood cultures were negative. The X-Ray of the thorax only showed signs of venous congestion.

clinician.final_diagnosis: ulcerated colonic carcinoma at the ileocecal valve
clinician.trajectory_summary: An elderly man presented acutely with bilateral leg weakness and chest pain with tachycardia. Initial physical exam found a systolic murmur without leg weakness, labs showed anemia, leukocytosis, and elevated CRP and creatinine. Echocardiography revealed continuous microcavitations in the right heart chambers. Chest CT showed hypodense hepatic lesions suspicious for metastasis, prompting concern for malignancy. Colonoscopy and biopsy of the ileocecal valve lesion were ordered to confirm diagnosis, but no documented histopathology or abdominal imaging reports were available in the source. No gastrointestinal symptom history or abdominal exam findings were documented. The diagnosis is supported primarily by clinical context, lab abnormalities, echocardiographic findings indicating an indwelling source of emboli or infection, and chest CT imaging implying metastatic disease consistent with an ulcerated colonic carcinoma at the ileocecal valve.
